reader_summary: This section explains how to choose a deliverable model after training. I need both evidence that the intended parameters were actually updated and separate evidence that answers work for the intended uses. Validation chooses among the unchanged base and corrections saved after 1,039 and 2,077 updates. The selected weights, data and generation settings are fixed before the final test. Through the new direct 20.6 link, I understand a LoRA candidate as a small learned correction branch whose output is added to the original fixed model’s output. Acceptance requires three things together: normal answer completion, retention thresholds for each use, and an agreed composite score strictly above the base. In the displayed 1,039-update example, photo descriptions improve from 16/28 to 23/28 and photo fact questions from 31/56 to 53/56, while chat with correct text falls from 4/4 to 2/4 and chat with actual ASR text falls from 3/4 to 2/4. Correct text bypasses recognition mistakes, so that decline exposes a problem in answering rather than allowing all blame to fall on hearing. Each correction also has three responses reaching the 384-new-token limit without normal ending. The new definition tells me that a token is a unit generated by the model and need not equal a Chinese character, so this is a generation budget rather than a count of Chinese characters. The longer correction also fails the chat threshold, and neither correction beats the composite rule. Retaining the base is a fallback under this rule, not a claim that it always answers correctly or completes normally. A demonstration prediction cost and an ending symbol each measure only part of what matters; complete generated content still needs checking. The reported full-training and validation numbers are earlier experiment results cited by the section, not runs I reproduced.

exercise.details: I answered the exercise again after the revised section and current prerequisites. Correct-transcript chat removes recognizer mistakes from that route; its decline from 4/4 to 2/4 therefore shows the answer component can regress even with correct text. Actual-ASR chat then assesses the combined route using the same real transcript across candidates, and it falls from 3/4 to 2/4. Photo gains cannot satisfy either chat route’s separate no-regression requirement, or replace the additional completion and strict-composite-improvement conditions. The section’s retention of a fallible base and postponement of final testing fit this rule. My new answer is saved in round2/exercise-answer.json; no model generation or training was run.

prerequisite_reader_summaries.20.7: The question and history remain inputs, but only the chosen assistant answer and ending directly contribute target costs. In the six-position Q/A sketch, the assistant boundary predicts A at target index 4; A then predicts end. Adding B creates a third scored target. prerequisite_reader_summaries.20.6: A candidate adds a trainable A/B correction to fixed W computation. A of shape 2 by 4 plus B of shape 3 by 2 gives 14 trainable numbers; rank=alpha=1 preserves scale alpha/r=1 and reduces that to 4+3=7. The earlier one-step toy runs printed those counts with an unchanged base and changed B. That proves the illustrated update scope in the toy run, not good natural-task answers.
